title: E. MEXimize the Score
statement:
Suppose we partition the elements of an array b into any number k of non-empty multisets S_1, S_2, …, S_k, where k is an arbitrary positive integer. Define the score of b as the maximum value of MEX(S_1)^{∗} + MEX(S_2) + … + MEX(S_k) over all possible partitions of b for any integer k.

Envy is given an array a of size n. Since he knows that calculating the score of a is too easy for you, he instead asks you to calculate the sum of scores of all 2^n - 1 non-empty subsequences of a.^{†} Since this answer may be large, please output it modulo 998,244,353.

^{∗}MEX of a collection of integers c_1, c_2, …, c_k is defined as the smallest non-negative integer x that does not occur in the collection c. For example, MEX([0,1,2,2]) = 3 and MEX([1,2,2]) = 0

^{†}A sequence x is a subsequence of a sequence y if x can be obtained from y by deleting several (possibly, zero or all) elements.

The first line contains an integer t (1 ≤ t ≤ 10^4) — the number of test cases.

The first line of each test case contains an integer n (1 ≤ n ≤ 2·10^5) — the length of a.

The second line of each test case contains n integers a_1, a_2, …, a_n (0 ≤ a_i < n) — the elements of the array a.

It is guaranteed that the sum of n over all test cases does not exceed 2·10^5.

For each test case, output the answer, modulo 998,244,353.

In the first testcase, we must consider seven subsequences:

In the last testcase, all subsequences have a score of 0.

Input:
```
430 0 140 0 1 150 0 1 2 241 1 1 1
```

Output:
```
11
26
53
0
```
